questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) She [have not finished] her lunch yet.
questions.explanation: Singular subject 'she' needs 'has' with the present perfect; 'yet' signals present perfect.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) The children [was playing] in the park when it started to rain.
questions.explanation: 'Children' is plural, so the past continuous needs 'were playing'.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) He is [more taller than] his brother.
questions.explanation: A one-syllable adjective forms its comparative with -er; the double comparative 'more taller' is wrong.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) I look forward [to see you] at the wedding.
questions.explanation: In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition, so a gerund follows: 'to seeing'.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) He [did not went] to office yesterday.
questions.explanation: After 'did not' the verb takes its base form: 'did not go'.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) [Walking along the road, a snake bit the old man.]
options: Walking along the road, the old man was bitten by a snake.
Walking along the road, a snake was biting the old man.
Walking along the road, the snake's bite hurt the old man.
questions.explanation: An opening participle phrase must describe the subject that follows. Only the old man can be walking, so he must be the subject.
questions.shortcut: Participle phrase -> its doer must come right after the comma.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) Everyone in the office [were] invited to the party.
questions.explanation: 'Everyone' is singular and takes a singular verb: 'was invited'.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) If I [would have known] the truth, I would have told you.
questions.explanation: Third conditional: 'if + past perfect, would have + past participle'. The if-clause cannot contain 'would have'.
questions.shortcut: if + had + pp, would have + pp.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) He [said me that] he would come late.
questions.explanation: 'Say' is not followed directly by a person; 'tell' takes a direct object: 'told me that'.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) She [is working] in this company since 2018.
questions.explanation: 'Since' with a point of time and an action continuing to now requires the present perfect continuous.
questions.shortcut: since / for + continuing action -> has / have been + -ing.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) He [suggested me] to take rest.
questions.explanation: 'Suggest', 'propose' and 'recommend' cannot take 'object + to-infinitive'; 'advise' can.
questions.shortcut: advise / ask / tell + me + to; suggest never.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) Rahul as well as his friends [are] coming to the party.
questions.explanation: With 'as well as' the verb agrees with the first subject, Rahul (singular): 'is coming'.
questions.shortcut: as well as: first subject decides.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) [Despite of] the heavy rain, the match continued.
questions.explanation: 'Despite' is never followed by 'of'; 'in spite of' is the form with 'of'.
questions.shortcut: Despite = in spite of (no 'of' after despite).

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) She gave the beggar [an one-rupee coin].
questions.explanation: 'One' begins with the consonant sound /w/, so 'a' is used; a compound adjective before a noun stays singular.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) He is the [taller of the three] brothers.
questions.explanation: For comparison among three or more, the superlative is used: 'tallest of the three'.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) Of the two sisters, Meena is [the more intelligent].
questions.explanation: For two persons, the comparative with 'the' ('the more intelligent') is correct; the superlative is for three or more.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) I [have seen him] yesterday at the market.
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' fixes a definite past time, so the simple past is required.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) The man [whom I thought was honest] cheated me.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun is the subject of 'was honest' ('I thought' is parenthetical), so the subject form 'who' is needed.
questions.shortcut: Who = subject of the verb that follows.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) He [don't like] spicy food.
questions.explanation: Third person singular in the present takes 'does not' + base verb.
questions.shortcut: he / she / it -> doesn't + base verb.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) There [is] many books on the shelf.
questions.explanation: 'There' is followed by a verb that agrees with the real subject 'books' (plural): 'There are'.
questions.shortcut: There + verb agrees with the noun after it.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) Neither Asha nor Meena [have] finished the work.
questions.explanation: 'Neither ... nor' takes a singular verb when both subjects are singular.
questions.shortcut: Neither-nor with singular nouns -> singular verb.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) This is the [most easiest] way to solve it.
questions.explanation: A superlative takes either 'most' + base adjective or the -est ending, never both.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) I am [use to] waking up early.
questions.explanation: The adjective phrase 'be used to' (accustomed to) is followed by a gerund; the form needs the -d.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) [Because of he was late], he missed the train.
questions.explanation: 'Because of' and 'due to' are followed by a noun; a full clause requires 'because'.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) She asked me [where was I going].
questions.explanation: In reported questions the word order is that of a statement: subject before verb, and the tense shifts to the past.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) The prices of vegetables [has risen] sharply this month.
questions.explanation: The subject 'prices' is plural, so 'have risen' is needed (past participle of rise is risen).

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) Unless you [do not work] hard, you will fail.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' already means 'if ... not', so the verb must be positive to avoid a double negative.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) He [as well as his sons were] arrested.
options: as well as his sons was
as well as his sons are
questions.explanation: With 'as well as' the verb agrees with the first subject 'he' and the tense stays past: 'was arrested'.
questions.shortcut: as well as: first subject; keep the tense.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) Had he studied harder, he [would pass] the exam.
questions.explanation: An inverted 'Had he studied' is a third conditional; the main clause takes 'would have + past participle'.
questions.shortcut: Had + subject + pp -> would have + pp.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) The Prime Minister, along with his ministers, [have] arrived.
questions.explanation: 'Along with' does not alter the number; the subject is 'the Prime Minister' (singular).

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) She is too tired to walk any further.
questions.explanation: 'Too ... to' is the correct pattern expressing an unwanted result; the bracket-free sentence is already right.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) I [am knowing] him since childhood.
questions.explanation: 'Know' is a stative verb (no continuous form) and 'since' requires the present perfect: 'have known'.
questions.shortcut: Stative verbs: no -ing; since -> present perfect.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) He [prevented me to go] there.
questions.explanation: 'Prevent' takes 'from + gerund': 'prevented me from going'.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) [Scarcely he had] entered the room when the phone rang.
questions.explanation: 'Scarcely' at the start requires inversion of auxiliary and subject: 'Scarcely had he entered'.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) The boy [who's bag] was stolen reported it to the police.
questions.explanation: The possessive relative pronoun for a person is 'whose' ('who's' = 'who is').

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) She [did a mistake] in the calculation.
questions.explanation: The fixed collocation is 'make a mistake' (not 'do').

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) He gave me [a good advice] before the interview.
questions.explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable: no 'a' and no plural -s.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) He prefers cycling [than walking].
questions.explanation: 'Prefer' is followed by 'to', not 'than': prefer X to Y.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) [Having been completed the work,] the engineers left the site.
questions.explanation: The engineers did the work, so the active participle 'having completed' is needed; the passive 'been completed' cannot take an object.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) It is high time you [start] preparing for the exam.
questions.explanation: 'It is high time' is followed by a past-tense verb (a present need expressed with the past).
questions.shortcut: It is (high) time + subject + past tense.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) I wish I [was] a bird so that I could fly.
questions.explanation: After 'wish' an unreal present wish takes the subjunctive 'were' for every person.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) He [does not hardly speak] to anyone.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly' is already negative; adding 'not' creates a double negative.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) [Each of the players have] received a medal.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular and takes 'has'; 'of the players' needs the plural noun.
questions.shortcut: Each of + plural noun + singular verb.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) She [cannot but to admire] his courage.
questions.explanation: 'Cannot but' is followed by the bare infinitive: 'cannot but admire'.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) No sooner did he reach home [when] it began to rain.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner' is paired with 'than'; 'hardly / scarcely' pair with 'when'.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) Water [boil] at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
questions.explanation: A scientific fact takes the simple present, and the singular subject 'water' needs -s.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) The student, together with his parents, [are] meeting the principal tomorrow.
questions.explanation: 'Together with' does not change the number of the subject; 'the student' is singular: 'is meeting'.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. (If the sentence is already correct, choose No improvement.) Mohan [as well as his brother has] won a scholarship.
options: as well as his brother have
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the first subject Mohan: 'has'. The sentence is already correct.
questions.shortcut: as well as: first subject; singular here.
